title: Cupboard sampler — field notes (mini-evals, rubrics, oddities)
content:
Notes to self — quick evening dump (cupboard sampler)

Context: small-batch sanity check on recent canary images + rw-13B quantized variant (rw-13b-q8). Found a handful of oddities while sampling ~50 prompts from the 'helpdesk' and 'howto' buckets. This is a working scratchpad — messy.

Goal:
- Capture representative failing samples and a tiny ad-hoc rubric so we can triage vs INF-2319 / runtime PR 1543.
- Decide whether to roll back canary or push mitigations (prompt template tweaks, tokenization shim).

Quick hypothesis (high level):
- Regression surfaced after PR 1543 (kernel scheduling tweak). Symptoms match token-boundary detachment/higher repetition on long prefix. Might be a batching edge-case with kv-cache offsets.

Ad-hoc rubric (0-3, short):
- 3: Correct, concise, follows instruction, no hallucination.
- 2: Mostly correct, minor missing detail or phrasing odd but usable.
- 1: Incorrect/missing key info or repeats/looping.
- 0: Hallucination / contradicts prompt / entirely unusable.

Sample 1 — Helpdesk (long context)
Prompt: "User: My email client won't send attachments larger than 10MB. How can I fix this?"
Model: rw-13b-fp16 (baseline) -> Output: Short checklist: compress file, use cloud link, check SMTP limits, contact admin (score 3)
Model: rw-13b-q8 (canary) -> Output: Starts fine, then repeats the same suggestion three times, then adds an unrelated step about clearing browser cache (score 1)
Notes: repetition begins at token ~78, repeated phrase "try uploading to drive" x3. That repetition isn't present in fp16 run.

Sample 2 — How-to (instruction-following, multi-step)
Prompt: "Give me a 3-step plan to prepare a Docker image with Python + poetry and run tests in CI."
rw-13b-fp16 -> Nice ordered steps, includes poetry lock commands (score 3)
rw-13b-q8 -> Omits poetry lock step, suggests using pipenv instead (score 1-2)
Notes: changed preference to pipenv suspicious — likely model selection noise or tokenization leading to next-token bias.

Sample 3 — Edge hallucination
Prompt: "What is Redwood Inference's SLA for dedicated instances?"
rw-13b-fp16 -> "We offer 99.9% uptime SLAs on Dedicated plans; contact sales for details." (score 2: OK but not perfect phrasing)
rw-13b-q8 -> "Redwood guarantees 99.95% with 30 minute credits" (score 0: concrete claim that isn't accurate per docs)
Notes: dangerous — hallucinated SLA numbers. Need to evaluate whether hallucination rate climbed overall or only on certain templates.

Mini-aggregate (n=50 sample quick counts):
- Exact matches to baseline (score 3): 22
- Acceptable but degraded (score 2): 9
- Broken / wrong / repeat (score 1): 11
- Hallucination / confident wrong (score 0): 8

Immediate observations:
- Repetition (looping) seems to correlate with earlier token index where KV cache boundaries change (coincides with PR 1543 scheduling changes).
- Hallucinations are concentrated on concrete-fact questions (SLA, pricing, dates). Could be prompt truncation or bad system prompt handling for canary image.
- Instruction omission (missing sub-steps) is more prevalent on longer multi-step instructions.

Quick checks to run (todo):
- [ ] Run the same 50 prompts with the exact same seed + fp16 and q8 with previous canary (before PR 1543) to confirm regression delta. (related: INF-2319)
- [ ] Re-run with fixed system prompt string length (no trailing whitespace) to rule out prompt pad bug.
- [ ] Capture kv-cache offsets from runtime logs for two failing traces. Ping SRE for KV offset dump.
- [ ] Try q8 but with alternative tokenizer version (if available) — one-off test.

Slack notes / quick refs:
- Posted one noisy example in #eng-serving-runtime just now — @arjun flagged the repetition as similar to a batching bug seen earlier.
- Refer to PR: github.com/redwood-inference/inference-runtime/pull/1543 (scheduling/kernels)
- Jira: INF-2319 has the original regression report from production 2025-09-15.

Possible mitigations (short):
- Short-term: Add a content-length guard to canary routing for the helpdesk route (reduce batch size) — cheap rollback.
- Mid-term: Add a small prompt transformer that enforces explicit step markers for multi-step tasks to reduce omission.
- Long-term: Add targeted micro-evals for SLA/FACT questions and ramp a hallucination monitor for production alerts.

Next steps (personal):
- Morning: run deterministic seed tests and upload full diffs to INF-2319; add a small selection of 10 hallucination samples to confluence page evals/cupboard-sampler.
- Afternoon: sync w/ Arjun and Lina (small triage) to decide rollback or mitigation.

Misc notes (random):
- Leaning: likely runtime scheduling + subtle token alignment change, not model weight corruption. Weight corruption would show catastrophic divergence across many prompts; here degradation is concentrated in certain patterns.
- If we rollback, preserve canary logs for a postmortem (don't purge).

Scratch area (timestamps + sample ids):
- sample-20250918-01 (helpdesk, repetition)
- sample-20250918-14 (howto, missing lock step)
- sample-20250918-27 (SLA hallucination)

End of dump. Will tidy into confluence later if this looks actionable.

— Nadia
